title: Discovery, proposals and proof: run positioning as a practice

say: Discovery, proposals and proof: run positioning as a practice.
This is the video for module three of Brand Strategy and Positioning.

Clients usually arrive saying, we need a new logo, or we need to go viral. Discovery is your chance to understand the business before agreeing. The right diagnosis protects the client's money and your reputation.

panel.heading: Clients arrive with a solution in mind
items: Clear packages make work easy to buy

say: Then clear packages, clear limits, and honest results turn your skill into a practice clients trust.

panel.heading: Clients arrive with a solution in mind
items: Clear packages make work easy to buy

say: Send a six-question form a day before. On the call, start by explaining the purpose: to understand, not to sell.

panel.heading: A 45-minute discovery agenda
items: 0 to 5: purpose is to understand, not sell

say: Spend most of the time on the business and its customers, then competitors. Who are your best customers? When you lose a sale, who wins it? Let short silences sit, because owners often add the most useful detail after a pause.

panel.heading: A 45-minute discovery agenda
items: 0 to 5: purpose is to understand, not sell

say: Ask: if this works, what will be different in six months? Then tell them when your proposal will arrive.

panel.heading: A 45-minute discovery agenda

say: For example, Chioma owns a cake shop in Enugu. Sales fell for six months, and she asks for a new logo and name. Ask why, gently. Fewer repeat orders. Why? Customers complained.

panel.heading: The cake shop that wanted a rebrand
items: Why did sales fall? Fewer repeat orders
Why? Thinner boxes, a new rider
Why? To save about 500 naira an order

say: She checks WhatsApp: 9 of the last 30 orders had complaints, and 7 of those 9 were cakes arriving damaged.

panel.heading: The cake shop that wanted a rebrand
items: Why did sales fall? Fewer repeat orders
Why? Thinner boxes, a new rider
Why? To save about 500 naira an order

say: Why? She switched to cheaper, thinner boxes and a new rider, to save about 500 naira an order.
The root cause is packaging, not the logo. A new logo would have cost money and changed nothing. So fix delivery first, then position on arrives perfect.

panel.rule: If the problem is not branding, say so clearly and in writing.

say: Strategy is thinking work, so clients cannot see it like a cake or a dress. Clear packages make it easy to buy. Amaka divides 600,000 naira by 60 hours: her minimum rate is 10,000 naira an hour.
A Sprint is about 12 hours. She adds 15 percent for meetings and revisions, and rounds to 140,000. A Full Project of 30 hours becomes 350,000.
A monthly retainer of 8 hours is 80,000 naira.
Her rate is a floor, not the price. If a clearer position could add 960,000 naira a year for a client like Bisi, 350,000 is easy to explain. She explains price with value, not hours.
Most project problems come from vague scope. Write limits into the proposal: for example eight interviews, three routes, two revision rounds, and no logo design or adverts.

cards.d: Say how many interviews, routes and revisions, and what is not included, like logos.
Extra asks get a written note with hours, fee and new date. Wait for a yes.
50% deposit first. Confirm it in your own app. Never ask for or share passwords, PINs or OTPs.

say: When the client asks for more, send a short written change request with the extra hours, fee and new deadline. If they say the price is too high, offer a smaller scope, not a cut price for the same work.

say: Work starts only after a signed agreement and a 50 percent deposit. Confirm every payment in your own app, because screenshots can be faked. Never ask clients for passwords, PINs or OTPs.

say: A workshop helps a team own the position. Invite the owner and two to five key staff, including riders and sales attendants, who often know customers best. Start with the goal, then the customer evidence.

panel.heading: A two-hour positioning workshop
items: Goal of the session and ground rules
Agree what to test, and who does what

say: Everyone writes possible differences, and each person gets three dots to vote. Pairs draft two statements. End by agreeing what to test, and send the actions in writing the same day.

panel.heading: A two-hour positioning workshop
items: Goal of the session and ground rules
Agree what to test, and who does what

say: Agree measures before launch, so you can compare. Tolu logs enquiries and orders. Before the new position, 10 of 40 enquiries became orders, 25 percent. Three months after, 15 of 45, about 33 percent.

panel.heading: Tolu's laundry, three months later
items: Note other changes, like a new estate

say: Her average order rose from 3,500 to 4,900 naira, because customers send all their work shirts at once. Discount requests fell from 6 to 2 a month.

panel.heading: Tolu's laundry, three months later
items: Note other changes, like a new estate

say: She also notes a new estate opened nearby, so she does not credit everything to the brand. That honesty is what makes a case study believable.

panel.heading: Tolu's laundry, three months later
items: Note other changes, like a new estate
panel.rule: Claim only results you measured. Label practice projects as practice.

say: To remember. Discovery finds the real problem. Ask why until you reach a cause you can act on. Your hourly rate is a floor, so explain price with value. Write scope limits and use change requests. And report only results you measured.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Ask why until the cause is actionable
Your rate is a floor; explain value
Write scope limits and change requests

say: Now build your discovery pack and write a half-page summary. Price your packages and write a proposal. Then write an honest case study, and a 90-day plan to win your first paid Sprint.
